title: Human iPSC-derived neurons stimulated with IFNγ present HLA class I-restricted antigens to cytotoxic CD8+ T cells
sections_read: Abstract; Results Figures 1-5; Materials and Methods; Data availability; publisher supplementary PDF (4 pages)
measured_variables: HLA-I IP-LC-MS/MS in human iPSC neural aggregates and matched fibroblasts across four donors; vehicle and IFNγ 100 ng/mL for 72 h; separate 0-72 h matched single-nucleus RNA-seq time course; HLA and IFNGR measures; selected T-cell injury assays
derived_variables: HLA binding/allotype predictions; neuron-enriched source-protein annotation; pooled cell-level module scores
prior_art_overlap: Directly establishes IFNγ-associated normal neural ligandome distinct from matched fibroblasts and baseline HNAs, plus antigen-dependent injury using engineered exogenous viral epitopes; it does not test cancer-restricted target lists or a tumor-therapy selection rule
exact_unanswered_contrast: Do resting-reference cancer-restricted peptide sequences appear in independently measured IFNγ-exposed nonmalignant HLA ligandomes, and can a fixed state-aware constraint predict held-out direct MS detections?
data_links: Publisher full text and 4-page Supplementary Material 1 PDF; no peptide-table repository accession identified; exact DOI searches on official PRIDE and MassIVE domains returned no indexed record
limits: Main article says datasets are not public and are available from corresponding author on reasonable request while deposition is being prepared; supplement has figures and donor HLA table but no peptide rows; mixed neural aggregate; only four IP-MS donors and deep coverage was not generated for all conditions

title: Pancreatic cancer-restricted cryptic antigens are targets for T cell recognition
sections_read: Main Results on cancer restriction and immunogenicity; Discussion limitations; Methods on PDO IFNγ exposure and target assays
measured_variables: LC-MS/MS in 11 IFNγ-treated PDAC PDOs; 28 healthy-tissue immunopeptidomics sources (229 samples), healthy thymus (5 samples), and Ribo-seq from 8 tissue types (49 samples); measured T-cell priming and endogenous PDO recognition
derived_variables: Cancer-restriction classification from evidence of translation or HLA presentation; target and HLA predictions
prior_art_overlap: Uses IFNγ to prepare tumor PDOs and applies resting/reference healthy-tissue evidence to target selection; explicitly states nonmalignant cell types or states may still translate/process/present CR peptides
exact_unanswered_contrast: No directly measured before/after inflammatory peptide list from nonmalignant cells is included in the reported cancer-restriction evaluation
data_links: PMC full text; supplement access previously recorded as blocked in cycle2 and not retried
limits: ncHLAp absence is bounded by coverage/detection; healthy tissue state history is not reported as paired inflammatory control; authors explicitly caution against ruling out unprofiled normal states

title: Unmasking the suppressed immunopeptidome of EZH2-mutated diffuse large B-cell lymphomas through combination drug treatment
sections_read: Methods on DLBCL cell lines, drugs and HLA ligand assays; Results on treatment-conditioned ligandomes and healthy-tissue filtering
measured_variables: Measured HLA-I/II ligands after decitabine, tazemetostat and IFNγ treatment of DLBCL cell lines; tumor-cell HLA expression and antigen-processing transcripts
derived_variables: Target source-protein selection by overlap across three lymphoma lines and absence from a published healthy-tissue source-protein list
prior_art_overlap: A close state-aware tumor-selection comparator, but all perturbation is on malignant lines; healthy reference is not an independently measured inflammatory normal-cell challenge and selection is mostly source-protein-level
exact_unanswered_contrast: Whether proposed tumor-restricted peptides remain undetected in independently measured nonmalignant cells under a defined inflammatory state
data_links: PMC full text; source discusses supplemental peptide tables and comparison to published healthy tissue data
limits: Does not perturb normal cells; absence from a healthy atlas is not proof of no presentation in an inflamed state; no matched normal-cell antigen-presentation dataset

title: Interferon-α promotes HLA-B-restricted presentation of conventional and alternative antigens in human pancreatic β-cells
sections_read: Relevant article Results/Methods/data statements; official Supplementary Data 2 and 7 workbooks inspected
measured_variables: Paired basal vs IFNα 2000 U/mL for 18 h in ECN90 human β-cell line; 4 culture preparations per condition from one line; Data 2 has 784 selected conventional-peptide sequences with per-condition replicate detection fractions; Data 7 has 292 peptide strings and binary condition flags across Basal/CAR/IFNα/IFNα+CAR/IFNα+ONX
derived_variables: HLA restriction/rank predicted; cluster labels and source annotations derived; Data 7 presence flags are author-reported condition summaries
prior_art_overlap: The authors already report IFNα-associated HLA-B shifts, alternative/PTM peptides, β-cell source enrichment, and proteasome-associated clusters
exact_unanswered_contrast: Exact sequence join of Data 2's 784 selected rows to 74 JCI Table 5 sequences found 0; selected table is not exhaustive, so this does not establish absence. Data 7 has no sample/replicate keys and its inhibitor clusters are published results. No distinct fixed held-out test survived.
limits: One ECN90 line, not four donors; two primary non-diabetic islet preparations in the article are untreated only, not paired to IFNα; Data 2 is selected and lacks named replicate rows; Data 7 lacks replicate keys and contains the published 10-cluster inhibitor analysis; predicted HLA restriction is not direct restriction; nondetection is not absence or safety.
